To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a sublimation technique that enables us to measure the carbon isotope ratio of CO2 and mixing ratios from small bubbly ice core samples with high precision.
we developed a new sublimation method for the determination of δ13C and mixing ratios of N2O and CO2 from air trapped in bubble and clathrated ice cores.
we developed and tested a new technique for measuring CO2 concentrations, CO2 isotopes, and N2O concentrations from air trapped in polar ice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the extraction, separation and measurement of CO2 and N 18 O from ice core air bubbles and clathrate hydrates.
the development of a sublimation technique that allows for high-precision δ13CO2 and mixing ratio measurements on small bubbly, clathrated and partially clathrated ice samples from ice core drilling.
the development of an analytical method for high precision stable carbon and oxygen isotope analysis of CO2 from ice core samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method presented here is able to reproduce the δ13C values from bubble ice with high reproducibility and accuracy and that it is suitable to measure δ13C values of clathrate ice.
the new method allows the determination of δ13C, mixing ratios of CO2 and N 20 from ice core samples with high precision and reproducibility.
our new technique provides a high precision and high accuracy method for the determination of δ13CO2 and CO2/N2Os from air trapped in bubbly, clathrated or mixed ice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this new method is a powerful tool for the analysis of small ice core samples, which are often the only ones available for a given ice core.
we have successfully combined two methods, which have been used separately for decades, to provide a new tool for ice core research.
this new method is a powerful and versatile tool to determine the isotopic composition and mixing ratios of the two most important greenhouse gases CO2 and N20 in small ice samples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
this method is suitable for the determination of high-precision CO2 and N ₂ O mixing ratios as well as δ13C of air trapped in ice.
sublimation can be used for high precision δ13C measurements on bubble and clathrated ice samples, which are important in order to study the carbon cycle over the past millennia.
the sublimation method allows for a very accurate determination of CO2 and N  2 O concentrations from small ice core samples, even if they are clathrated or partially clathrated.
